justification: Adds a required falsifiable_check field to the QA report schema, enforced by scripts/qa_gate.py at critical and standard tiers. This changes the gate every future commit must pass, so it affects all subsequent work rather than one feature. No production data, no customer-facing surface, no schema change — standard rather than critical.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: any test fails, in particular the one asserting the gate still rejects the original DQ-30 verification claim; if that guard ever rots this goes red

pre_impl.existing_data: No database access at all: qa_gate.py reads a JSON report file and runs git and AST checks only. The only existing state it touches is .qa_report.json, which is ephemeral per commit.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Existing reports written before this change have no falsifiable_check field and will now be rejected at critical and standard tiers. That is the intended friction rather than a defect, but any in-flight branch must add the field before it can push.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Applies to every future report rather than retroactively; nothing already merged is re-validated. Minor tier is deliberately exempt so trivial changes do not train people to dismiss the gate.

functions.name: check_falsifiable
functions.input: The parsed QA report dictionary and the tier requirements dictionary, called from validate_report during section one validation.
functions.output: A list of human-readable error strings, empty when the report names both a runnable command and a distinct condition under which that command fails.
functions.if_none: When the tier does not require the check it returns an empty list immediately, and when the field is missing entirely it returns a single explanatory error naming the DQ-30 origin.

values.if_missing: The report is rejected with an explicit message showing the required shape, rather than silently passing as it would have before this change.

queries: N/A — this module performs no database queries.

break_it.scenario: Someone satisfies the field with a plausible but tautological check that the self-comparison regex does not happen to match, and the gate passes a non-verification.
break_it.what_happens: A change is marked verified on a check that cannot fail, which is precisely the DQ-30 defect recurring with different wording.
break_it.how: Partially, and deliberately so — detecting tautology in general is undecidable. The gate enforces the two properties whose absence caused the original failure: a runnable command and a red condition stated separately. The docstring says plainly that it is not a tautology detector, so it is not mistaken for one.
break_it.repro: Add a report whose command is a real script but whose fails_when restates the command's success condition, then run scripts/qa_gate.py and observe it pass.

break_it.scenario: The gate fires so often that developers paste a boilerplate falsifiable_check to get past it, and the field becomes decoration.
break_it.what_happens: Friction is added with no protection gained, and the reports become less trustworthy than before because they now carry a field that looks like evidence.
break_it.how: Minor tier is exempt, so routine copy and config changes never see it. It fires only where a real verification should exist, following the alarm-fatigue lesson recorded in DQ-34 and applied when dcp_all_provisions was removed from the zone validator's targets.
break_it.repro: Write a minor-tier report with no falsifiable_check and confirm scripts/qa_gate.py still passes it.

break_it.scenario: The self-comparison regex matches a legitimate check that merely contains the word drift, blocking valid work.
break_it.what_happens: A correct report is rejected and the author either rewords it needlessly or loses confidence in the gate.
break_it.how: The error text states the reasoning and explicitly offers the escape: state why the check is not self-referential. A false positive costs one sentence of justification, whereas a false negative costs a silently unverified fix, so the asymmetry is deliberate.
break_it.repro: Set fails_when to a sentence containing the word drift and confirm the message explains the escape rather than simply refusing.

post_merge.db_reset: No database change of any kind; this module never connects to Postgres.
post_merge.secrets: No new secrets or environment variables are introduced by this change.
post_merge.other_repo: No other repository or service needs updating; qa_gate.py is consumed only by .githooks/pre-push in this repository.
post_merge.manual_verify: Any branch already in flight must add a falsifiable_check to its report before it can push at critical or standard tier.
